title: Book: The Simple Path to Wealth — JL Collins (2016)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: JL Collins lays out a simple plan: spend less than you earn, avoid debt, invest the surplus in broad, low-cost index funds and hold through market ups and downs. He popularised the idea of 'F-you money', enough savings to walk away from a job you dislike, and urges readers not to try to time the market. The principles are widely shared by index-investing writers. Limits: the specific funds, accounts and tax rules are American; in India you would translate the idea to low-cost Indian index funds, EPF/PPF/NPS and local tax rules, and keep an emergency fund and insurance first. Not personal advice.
